claimsToVerify: Pyramid builders in Giza lived in purpose-built barracks or worker villages.
The mainstream archaeological consensus is that pyramid builders were recruited laborers, not slaves.
Worker graffiti shows crew names like 'Friends of Khufu' or 'Drunkards of Menkaure'.
Rations for pyramid workers included bread, beer, and garlic.
Archaeological evidence (skeletons with set bones) shows workers received medical treatment.
Ancient Egyptian workers went on strike (such as the famous strike under Ramesses III).
